articles.title: Nepal avalanche kills 15 workers at Himlung Himal camp, one still missing
articles.summary: At least 15 Nepali workers were killed after an avalanche buried a mountain camp they were preparing for foreign climbers in central Nepal, making it the
articles.body: At least 15 Nepali workers were killed after an avalanche buried a mountain camp they were preparing for foreign climbers in central Nepal, making it the deadliest incident of the country’s autumn climbing season, which ends this month.The avalanche struck the base camp of the 7,126-metre Himlung Himal in the northern Manang district over the weekend, burying workers who were pitching tents and fixing ropes ahead of the arrival of foreign climbers.Rescuers have recovered 15 bodies from the site, including eight retrieved from beneath the snow on Thursday and seven recovered earlier in the week, Tul Singh Gurung, president of the Nepal National Mountain Guide Association (NNMGA), told Reuters.“The bodies that were recovered today are expected to be brought by a helicopter to Kathmandu,” Gurung said.One worker remains missing, although Gurung said the chances of finding the person were dim and the rescue operation was likely to be wound up.Workers were preparing camp for foreign climbersThe foreign climbers had not yet reached the base camp when the avalanche struck.The camp was being prepared by expedition support staff for a 14-member all-women climbing group from a school in the UAE. The team was expected to arrive in Kathmandu on October 1.14 staff from Himalayan Holidays and two kitchen workers from Imagine Nepal Treks had initially been caught in the avalanche. Earlier reports had put the number of missing people lower before expedition organisers and authorities revised the figure after receiving information from the remote site.The avalanche hit after persistent rain and heavy snowfall in the Himlung Himal area. Rescue efforts were hampered by poor weather and difficult access to the base camp.Two bodies recovered earlier were identified by search team members as climbing guides Pasang Bhote and Chhebi Bhote.Deadliest incident of autumn climbing seasonThe Himlung Himal accident is the latest deadly incident involving high-altitude workers and climbers in the Himalayas and Karakoram this year.Nepal attracts thousands of visitors each year to its mountains, supporting tens of thousands of people who work as guides, porters and other expedition staff, as well as in tourism-related jobs.However, the work has become increasingly dangerous as climate change accelerates the melting of glaciers and ice.The avalanche has now become the deadliest incident of Nepal’s autumn climbing season, according to Reuters. Gurung said the recovery operation was expected to conclude after rescuers retrieved the latest eight bodies.The 7,126-metre Himlung Himal lies in the Nar Phu region of Manang district and is among the mountains that attract climbers during Nepal’s autumn expedition season.You use AI every day. articles.title: Father owned a £1.25 million Yorkshire property; daughter claimed part after his death, but court ruled in favour of his widow
articles.summary: A daughter's attempt to claim part of her late father's £1.25 million Yorkshire property has failed, after the High Court rejected her claims under his
articles.body: A daughter's attempt to claim part of her late father's £1.25 million Yorkshire property has failed, after the High Court rejected her claims under his will, the doctrine of proprietary estoppel and the Inheritance (Provision for Family and Dependants) Act 1975. The case, Hodgson v Hodgson [2026] EWHC 922 (Ch), was decided by HH Judge Davis-White KC in the Business and Property Courts in Leeds on 23 April 2026. Anthony Hodgson, known as Tony, died in October 2020 aged 74, leaving property at Slingsby, North Yorkshire. A jointly appointed valuation expert valued the property as a whole at £1,250,000 as of June 2025. His daughter, Jane Hodgson, argued that she was entitled to her father's half interest in part of the property under his will, or alternatively through proprietary estoppel or the Inheritance Act 1975. The judge rejected all three claims.Hodgson v Hodgson case: why the High Court rejected Jane Hodgson's claim to part of the family propertyAt the centre of the dispute was Tony's will, made on 23 March 2016. Jane argued that a clause leaving her father's interest in his remaining real property and land entitled her to his half share in the area of the farm she had been using, known in the judgment as Jane's Land. The judge disagreed after considering the wording of the will alongside the surrounding circumstances. He found that the will first provided for Tony's residue to pass to his wife, Joyce, and that the gifts of specific areas of land to Jane and her brother James would only operate if Joyce failed to survive Tony. Because Joyce survived her husband, those substitute gifts did not take effect. The judge also found that the property at issue, apart from Wyville Hall, had been held by Tony and Joyce as joint tenants in law and equity immediately before Tony's death. That meant Tony's interest passed to Joyce by survivorship rather than forming part of his estate.The judgment also examined earlier discussions about the couple's wills. Solicitors' attendance notes from 2013 and 2015 recorded different plans for dividing the property between their children after both parents had died. By October 2015, however, the notes recorded that Tony and Joyce intended to leave their estates to each other first, with land then passing to James and Jane after the surviving parent died. The judge considered those documents alongside the final wording of Tony's 2016 will when determining what it meant.Jane Hodgson's proprietary estoppel claim fails over alleged promises about the farmJane also argued that she should receive an interest in the property under proprietary estoppel. She said Tony had told her around 1993 that the farm would one day be hers and that she should make her life there. She also relied on assurances from Joyce that she would eventually inherit the property she had lived and worked on. Jane said she had relied on those assurances by working on the farm, increasing the number of animals she kept, opening it to paying visitors, claiming agricultural subsidies, letting parts of the land to other people and contributing to work at the farmhouse. She also argued that she had not pursued other career options and had not made pension provision because of the expectation that she would eventually inherit the property.The judge accepted that Joyce had made promises to Jane about her eventually inheriting part of the property and found those promises sufficiently clear for the first element of a proprietary estoppel claim. However, he found that Jane had failed to establish the necessary causal detrimental reliance. The judgment noted that Jane had been given the farm business and had operated it while living rent-free at the farmhouse and using the land without paying rent. She also received income from agricultural subsidies and from letting part of the arable land. The judge concluded that, even if Jane had relied on the promises, the disadvantages she claimed had to be considered alongside the benefits she had received. He ultimately found that there was no overall detriment caused by reliance on the promises.Daughter's Inheritance Act claim over the family property also failsJane's final claim was brought under the Inheritance (Provision for Family and Dependants) Act 1975, which allows certain family members to seek reasonable financial provision from a deceased person's estate. The judge rejected Jane's claim under the Act, alongside her arguments under the will and proprietary estoppel. The ruling therefore left her without the property interest she had sought from her father's estate. The property at the centre of the dispute covers 32.825 acres and includes Wyville Farm, farmland and a number of buildings. A jointly appointed expert valued the property as a whole at £1.075 million as of October 2020 and £1.25 million as of June 2025. The judgment separately considers Wyville Hall and James's Land in determining how the various interests in the property were held and what happened to them after Tony's death.In its final conclusions, the court found that the relevant property, excluding Wyville Hall, had been held by Tony and Joyce as joint tenants in law and equity immediately before Tony's death. Tony's 2016 will also provided for his residue to pass to Joyce, while the specific gifts of Jane's Land and James's Land were conditional on Joyce predeceasing him. Jane's proprietary estoppel claim failed because she had not established the required causal detrimental reliance, while her claim under the Inheritance Act 1975 also failed. The case illustrates the difficulty of establishing a claim to family property where informal promises conflict with later legal documents and the ownership structure of the land. In reaching his decision, the judge considered Tony's final will, earlier solicitor's attendance notes, the legal ownership of the property and the evidence surrounding Jane's alleged reliance on promises about her future inheritance.What happens to the £1.25 million Yorkshire propertyThe property at the centre of the dispute covers around 32.825 acres and includes Wyville Farm, farmland and a number of buildings. The jointly appointed expert, Ashley Dodgson of GSC Greys, valued the property as a whole at £1.075 million as of October 2020 and £1.25 million as of June 2025. The valuation included separate assessments for parts of the property, including the farmhouse, Stackyard, farm buildings and fields. In his final conclusions, Judge Davis-White KC held that the property, leaving aside Wyville Hall, was held by Tony and Joyce as joint tenants in law and equity immediately before Tony's death. He also confirmed that Tony's 2016 will gave the residue of his estate to Joyce and that the specific gifts of Jane's Land and James's Land would only operate if Joyce had died before him. Jane's proprietary estoppel claim failed because she had not established causal detrimental reliance, while her Inheritance Act claim also failed.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Full-body scanners at airports: Govt tests tech & algorithms to address privacy concerns before wider rollout
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India's aviation security regulator is collecting data from ongoing trials of full-body scanners at Bengaluru and Cochin airports before
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India's aviation security regulator is collecting data from ongoing trials of full-body scanners at Bengaluru and Cochin airports before deciding on their wider deployment, with the technology's algorithms also being refined to account for objects commonly worn by passengers in India.Bureau of Civil Aviation Security (BCAS) Director General Rajesh Nirwan told reporters on Thursday that full-body scanners have been mandated at eight airports, while trials are currently being conducted at Bengaluru and Cochin. Authorities are collecting data from the trials, including the number of alarms generated, which will be assessed before a decision is taken on introducing the scanners at airports.However, Cochin is not among the eight airports where the scanners have been mandated.The deployment of full-body scanners has been delayed for years, partly due to concerns over passenger privacy. Nirwan said newer scanners are being made “image agnostic”, meaning they do not produce an actual image of the passenger but instead display a model and identify the specific part of the body where a suspicious object may have been detected, reported PTI.BCAS is also working with scanner vendors and original equipment manufacturers to refine the technology for Indian conditions, including concerns that jewellery and other commonly worn items could trigger alarms.“What we are getting today in India is based on algorithms that have been designed for foreign markets. There are certain typical things that are on the body of Indian citizens or people living in India. So, those algorithms are also being continuously refined,” Nirwan said.The data collected during the ongoing trials will be used to further refine the algorithms, he added.Meanwhile, the officials also addressed the recent Flydubai cockpit attack in which Indian pilot Smit Machchhar was injured, saying Indian aviation authorities are examining the incident and will hold internal deliberations on whether any aviation security advisory is required.Civil Aviation Secretary Samir Kumar Sinha said the matter was under examination and any decision on an advisory would be taken after internal discussions. “... in case some advisory is to be issued, obviously we will put it up to the higher authorities for taking a decision on that,” Sinha said.The comments came a day after Flydubai flight FZ1073, flying from Dubai to Tel Aviv with 174 passengers, was diverted to Saudi Arabia after an altercation in the cockpit. Indian captain Smit Machchhar was seriously injured while trying to tackle his co-pilot, and the aircraft later landed safely at Tabuk.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: In 2018, Rihanna’s foundation began preparing Caribbean clinics for hurricanes with solar power; the work now spans climate resilience
articles.summary: For many people, Rihanna’s public profile is tied to music, fashion and the global reach of Fenty Beauty.
articles.body: For many people, Rihanna’s public profile is tied to music, fashion and the global reach of Fenty Beauty. Her philanthropic work has developed on a different track. Since 2012, the Clara Lionel Foundation has funded projects spanning health, education, women’s entrepreneurship, culture and climate resilience, with more than $100 million directed towards work in the Caribbean, the United States and East Africa. Some of its climate work has focused on a practical problem familiar across the Caribbean: keeping essential health services operating when hurricanes strike. That approach took shape in 2018, after successive destructive storm seasons, when the foundation began supporting health with stronger infrastructure and solar power systems.Rihanna’s foundation adds solar power to hurricane-ready clinicsThe foundation’s Caribbean health programme grew out of a shift towards preparing medical facilities before disasters happen. Rather than limiting assistance to the aftermath of a hurricane, the work has included improvements intended to help clinics remain functional when electricity supplies, buildings and other infrastructure are damaged, as reported by Clara Lionel Foundation (CLF).Solar power became part of that effort. Health centres can depend heavily on reliable electricity for lighting, refrigeration, communications and medical equipment, making power failures particularly disruptive during severe weather. Supporting renewable energy systems therefore formed part of a broader effort to make clinics more resilient.The initiative began in 2018, after two particularly destructive hurricane seasons in the Caribbean. The work focused on strengthening healthcare infrastructure while giving facilities an alternative source of electricity when conventional power networks were disrupted.What began Rihanna’s philanthropic journeyThe Clara Lionel Foundation was established by Rihanna after the death of her grandmother from complications related to cancer. It was named after her grandparents, Clara and Lionel, and its earliest work was closely connected to healthcare.The foundation’s first major act was to provide the hospital where her grandmother had received treatment with a modern radiotherapy machine. From there, its work expanded considerably. Healthcare remained an important part of its portfolio, but funding also moved into education, arts and culture, women’s economic opportunities and disaster preparedness.Over time, the organisation built a team that included global health specialists and policy professionals. As reported by CLF Annual Report 2022 and Forbes respectively, its work has also brought partnerships with organisations and philanthropists outside Rihanna’s own foundation, including Twitter co-founder Jack Dorsey (#StartSmall) and Jay-Z’s Shawn Carter Foundation.How Rihanna’s foundation is preparing clinics for disastersThe foundation has also provided large-scale assistance when crises have already taken place. According to Associated Press (AP), during the COVID-19 pandemic, it distributed more than $33 million towards emergency response and related efforts.That experience sits alongside the longer-term preparedness work. There is a distinction between replacing what a hurricane has destroyed and making a clinic less vulnerable before the next storm arrives. The Caribbean programme has increasingly reflected the latter approach, with infrastructure upgrades and solar energy intended to give healthcare facilities more capacity to operate during disruption.Melissa revealed the limits of preparing healthcare facilities aloneThe need for that preparation became particularly clear after Hurricane Melissa struck the Caribbean last October. The storm was among the strongest Atlantic hurricanes to make landfall, and Jamaica experienced widespread disruption.The clinics reinforced through the foundation’s earlier programme had not yet extended to Jamaica when Melissa arrived. According to the United Nations in the Caribbean, more than 279,000 people remained displaced five weeks after the storm, while five major hospitals in Jamaica sustained severe damage.The foundation has since launched the Rebuild & Reimagine Fund to support recovery in Jamaica, Haiti and other Caribbean islands affected by Hurricane Melissa. Its focus includes health, water and education. The response also illustrates the limits of preparing individual facilities in isolation. A clinic may have stronger walls or its own solar generation, but patients still depend on functioning hospitals, roads, water systems and other services beyond the facility itself.Rihanna’s philanthropy combines disaster response with long-term climate resilienceRihanna’s philanthropic work now covers two sides of disaster management. The foundation has continued to provide money after major emergencies, while its earlier investments in Caribbean clinics show a longer-term interest in reducing the effects of future storms.The solar-powered clinic model is one example of that approach. It combines an immediate infrastructure need, reliable electricity, with a broader climate adaptation strategy. For health facilities operating in hurricane-prone regions, keeping basic services running can depend as much on preparation carried out months or years beforehand as it does on emergency funding after a storm.The foundation’s work in Jamaica is now adding another layer to that effort, with health, water and education included in its recovery plans. What began with a healthcare-focused response to a family loss has therefore developed into a wider programme covering both emergency assistance and preparation for increasingly disruptive climate events.You use AI every day. articles.title: Smit-ten: World in love with heroic Indian pilot who saved Israelis and beat social media hijacking
articles.summary: TOI correspondent from Washington: The old saying that lies go halfway across the world before truth gets its shoes on was on full display in the hours
articles.body: TOI correspondent from Washington: The old saying that lies go halfway across the world before truth gets its shoes on was on full display in the hours after the Fly Dubai hijacking episode. What began as a genuine mid-air emergency on flydubai Flight FZ1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv rapidly spawned a swirl of inaccurate claims, misidentifications, and social-media distortions, and it wasn’t until Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu went public with details of the heroic act by the pilot, Capt Smit Macchchar, whom he clearly identified as Indian, that the world began to acknowledge an extraordinary feat of courage.Even US President Donald Trump briefly acknowledged the bravery of the pilot before digressing into a vivid description of how the attacker was taken down by Israeli passengers. “The pilot, in bad shape, had the sense to open the door!” Trump said, calling him a “hero” and adding, “it seems as though the copilot was perhaps a terrorist or perhaps a whack job”.The MAGA boss later used the episode to shill for Boeing on his Truth Social platform, posting, “Congratulations to the GREAT Boeing Company for producing a plane, the 737 Max, that was able to withstand G Forces and Strain far beyond what it was designed and expected to do. It was an amazing show of precise and powerful structural planning and design.”“It is about time that The Boeing Company, which builds, by far, the finest commercial airliners in the sky, was given credit for this airplane’s incredible “genius!” To Kelly Ortberg, and all of his officers and associates at Boeing, congratulations on a job well done!!!” Trump, chief spokesman for American products, wrote.However, many experts acknowledged that but for the heroism of the Indian pilot and the Israeli plumber, who led the passenger effort to subdue the hijacker co-pilot, the plane, regardless of how it was built, may have been dust in the desert. Professional pilots emphasized how extraordinarily difficult Captain Machchhar's situation was due to post-9/11 reinforced cockpit door protocols, which have resulted in cockpit doors being armored and locked to prevent outside entry.Pilots pointed out that Machchhar fighting through stab wounds to manually override and unlock the door was the single critical move that allowed off-duty pilots and passengers to breach the cockpit and save the aircraft. Aviators also lauded Machchhar's muscle memory and tactical awareness – squawking the hijacking emergency code, resisting the co-pilot's attempts to put the Boeing 737 into a dive, and unlocking the door before losing consciousness or control. Many noted that when the aircraft entered a tailspin and lost altitude, Machchhar held onto the controls long enough to buy time for the door to be opened, calling his actions "a masterclass in airmanship under pressure.”Still, the initial hours after the attempted hijacking and crash saw much dust and distortions on social media. Early reporting and online speculation filled information gaps with errors. Some initial accounts and circulating posts described the event in ways that blurred whether it was an external hijacking, an internal cockpit struggle, or something else. Some outlets and social-media claims floated differing nationalities for the pilots, including identifying the captain who was stabbed as Emirati.As usual, social media vermin from Pakistan, where most of the world’s most wanted terrorists, from Osama bin Laden to Khalid Shaikh Mohammed, go to roost, jumped in with vile theories of an Indian-Israeli/RAW-Mossad plot. Some Pakistan-based accounts posted fabricated videos and claims linking a purported RAW operative named Raghav Menon to a plot.It wasn’t till Netanyahu himself went on air and confirmed the heroism of Capt Macchchar after ascertaining facts from flyers returning to Tel Aviv that the rest of the world, including Trump, acknowledged the Indian pilot’s role. “I hope the entire nation of India is proud of Capt Machchhar! He is a hero in Israel today!” the US ambassador to Israel, Mike Huckabee, said on Thursday.And indeed he is. “In honor of the Indian pilot who saved all the Israelis, I propose every Israeli order Indian food tomorrow. 10 million Indian lunches ordered tomorrow on Wolt (the Israeli version of Zomato/Swiggy. It's the least we can do,” David Keyes, a former spokesman & advisor to Netanyahu posted on X.“I'm starting a new airline. Just Indian pilots and Israeli passengers. articles.body: Iranian military on Thursday killed six members of a "terrorist" group in Zahedan, the capital city of the Sistan and Baluchistan province in southeastern Iran.The Sistan-Baluchistan province frequently sees clashes between security forces and armed Sunni-separatist groups and is a major drug trafficking route.The Iranian revolutionary guards had reportedly discovered and confiscated explosive packages from the "terrorists", IRNA news agency reported.However, Tehran did not identify the six people killed and gave no further information on the incident.On Wednesday, an explosion was reportedly heard in Zahedan with no reported damage, Fars news agency reported, citing the city's administrative office.Human rights group Haalvsh, which monitors Sistan-Baluchistan, said fighting between military and security forces and armed individuals had started on Thursday morning.Tehran accuses some armed groups of ties to foreign powers and involvement in cross-border smuggling, Reuters reported.Iran weighs US response to peace proposalThese developments emerged while Tehran considers Washington's reply to its most recent proposal for reviving the broken ceasefire.On Wednesday, the US response to Iran’s seven-day peace plan was formally delivered to Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian.Iranian government spokeswoman Fatemeh Mohajerani stated that foreign minister Abbas Araghchi was informed of the response through Qatari mediators, IRNA news agency reported. articles.title: Linda Evangelista first listed her New York penthouse for $9.45 million in 2024; after price cuts and a rental stint for Keanu Reeves, the West Chelsea home has now sold for $6.75 million
articles.summary: Linda Evangelista’s longtime West Chelsea penthouse has sold for $6.75 million after more than two years on and off the market.
articles.body: Linda Evangelista’s longtime West Chelsea penthouse has sold for $6.75 million after more than two years on and off the market. The supermodel first listed the home for $9.45 million in May 2024, but later reduced the asking price before briefly renting it to actor Keanu Reeves. Both the New York Post and CityRealty reported the closing. Evangelista bought the residence in 2001, when West Chelsea was still emerging as an arts district, and remained connected to the property as Manhattan’s skyline and luxury market changed around it.A purchase made before the High LineEvangelista purchased the penthouse in 2001 for $1.4 million, according to the New York Post. CityRealty, citing property records, reported a different figure of $8.4 million as the original purchase price, creating a discrepancy in published accounts. Regardless of the exact amount, the purchase came before West Chelsea experienced the development boom that reshaped the neighbourhood.The home is located in the Spears Building at 525 West 22nd Street, a six-storey condominium conversion of a former industrial building. Evangelista bought the property eight years before the first section of the High Line opened to the public, when the surrounding area had a more industrial and gallery-driven character.Over the years, the neighbourhood gained luxury towers, restaurants, art spaces and some of Manhattan’s most sought-after views. The penthouse’s location placed it close to the High Line, while its height and open design gave it the kind of privacy and scale that are unusual in a city apartment.A spacious industrial-chic interiorThe four-bedroom, two-bathroom penthouse spans approximately 4,022 square feet, according to the reports. Its interiors combine the raw features of a former industrial building with the comfort expected from a luxury residence.The apartment has high ceilings, skylights, exposed brick walls and polished concrete floors. These details preserve some of the building’s original character, while custom built-ins and large open rooms make the space more practical for modern living.The living room features a fireplace and generous proportions suitable for entertaining. A chef’s kitchen provides a central gathering point, with space for dining and preparation. The layout also allows the rooms to feel connected without losing the sense of privacy associated with a multi-bedroom home.The residence’s most dramatic feature may be its 2,500-square-foot terrace. Outdoor space is especially valuable in Manhattan, and a terrace of that size gives the apartment room for dining, lounging and hosting guests above the streets of West Chelsea.A bedroom designed for a supermodelThe corner primary bedroom suite has views towards the High Line and includes a spa-style bathroom. It also comes with an expansive dressing area and six custom closets that extend to the ceiling.The dressing space is a particularly fitting feature for Evangelista, who became one of the most recognisable supermodels of the 1990s. She was part of the celebrated group that included Naomi Campbell, Cindy Crawford, Christy Turlington, Claudia Schiffer and Tatjana Patitz.Evangelista’s career helped define the era when fashion models became global celebrities. Her home’s large dressing area offers a glimpse of how the apartment was tailored to her life, combining the practical demands of a fashion wardrobe with the dramatic proportions of the penthouse.Despite its celebrity associations, the property’s appeal is not limited to its former owner. The terrace, views, open floor plan and industrial details would also attract buyers looking for a distinctive primary residence or a large Manhattan base.Keanu Reeves rented the homeThe penthouse gained fresh attention when Keanu Reeves rented it while he was in New York performing in the Broadway production of Waiting for Godot. The New York Post reported that the actor paid approximately $45,000 per month.The rental period gave the residence a second celebrity connection during its time on the market. It also showed that the apartment could function as a temporary home for someone seeking privacy, space and a convenient location near Manhattan’s cultural districts.Reeves’ tenancy came as the apartment was being marketed for sale. Rather than remaining vacant, the property was used as a high-end rental while Evangelista and her representatives continued looking for a buyer.The arrangement also added another chapter to the home’s public profile. Evangelista had purchased it before the High Line became a major attraction, while Reeves occupied it after the neighbourhood had become one of New York’s most recognisable luxury addresses.Several price reductions before the saleEvangelista initially listed the penthouse for $9.45 million in May 2024. The asking price was later reduced to $8.19 million and then to $7.99 million earlier in 2026, according to the New York Post.The final sale price of $6.75 million was below the original asking price and lower than the later reductions. CityRealty described the transaction as a loss for Evangelista, based on its report that she had paid $8.4 million for the home.Listing agent Steve Gold of Corcoran previously described the eventual price as a value opportunity. He noted that some nearby properties had sold for more than $5,000 per square foot, a comparison that highlighted the penthouse’s large size and location.The sale reflects the difficulty of pricing celebrity-owned property in a changing luxury market. A famous owner can generate attention, but buyers still weigh layout, building amenities, outdoor space, views and the broader condition of the market.Evangelista remains in New YorkAlthough she has sold the West Chelsea penthouse, Evangelista is not leaving New York. The New York Post reported that she purchased a three-bedroom apartment at 35 Yards for $5.24 million in 2025.Her move marks a change of address rather than a departure from the city. The new apartment gives her a different setting, while the sale of the Spears Building residence closes a chapter that began when West Chelsea was still developing into the neighbourhood it is today.For the buyer, the $6.75 million purchase offers a large and distinctive home with a terrace, industrial architecture and a direct connection to New York’s fashion and entertainment history. For Evangelista, the transaction concludes a long real estate story that began before the High Line and ended after the apartment had briefly welcomed one of Hollywood’s most recognisable actors.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: In 1988, Fess Parker bought a 714-acre California ranch; decades later, the family venture spans vineyards, Wagyu cattle and hospitality, with his children and grandchildren carrying on the business
articles.summary: What started as a quiet retirement plan in California wine country has grown into a large family-owned farming and hospitality business.
articles.body: What started as a quiet retirement plan in California wine country has grown into a large family-owned farming and hospitality business. When actor Fess Parker bought the 714-acre Foxen Canyon Ranch in 1988, he planned to raise a small herd of cattle, plant a few acres of grapes, and start a small family winery. According to the official history on the Fess Parker Winery site, the former Hollywood star, best known for playing Davy Crockett and Daniel Boone, wanted to build a lasting family business that could be passed down through generations. Decades later, that first land purchase in Santa Barbara County has grown into a diverse group of businesses run directly by Parker's children and grandchildren. The enterprise includes award-winning vineyards, a high-end Wagyu cattle operation, boutique hospitality businesses, and a local craft brewery.Estate growth and winemaking achievementsThe family's wine business began in 1989 at Foxen Canyon Ranch along the Foxen Canyon Wine Trail. Over the years, the family added more vineyards to support full-scale wine production from its own estate. In 1995, Parker's son Eli Parker became head winemaker. In 2006, Eli Parker was named Winemaker of the Year at the San Francisco International Wine Competition for his work with estate-grown Rhone and Burgundian grape varieties. Today, the winery is still centered on its estate vineyard, Rodney's, which received Sustainability in Viticulture (SIP) certification in 2020. According to official site documents, the family has also added solar panels at its winemaking facility to reduce its use of outside energy and moved toward more sustainable packaging across its wine brands. In 2022, Wine & Spirits Magazine named Fess Parker Winery to its annual list of the Top 100 Wineries in the world.Grandchildren expand into cattle and hospitalityAs the business expanded, later generations took on leadership roles in different parts of the original estate. Katie Parker McDonald, one of Fess Parker's granddaughters, runs the FP Ranch Beef program with her husband, Rocky McDonald, a former professional bull rider. According to company history on the FP Ranch Beef website, the couple created a sustainable, grass-fed and sustainably finished Wagyu cattle operation on the family's home ranch in Los Olivos. The Wagyu operation uses DNA testing and selective breeding to manage the genetics of the herd. It produces beef ranging from USDA Prime Plus to Japanese A5 standards. Katie Parker McDonald also manages horseback trail rides on the ranch. Other family members run related businesses under the same corporate group. Fess Parker's daughter, Ashley Parker Snider, is a co-owner and manages sales and marketing with her husband, company president Tim Snider. Their adult children, Spencer and Greer, have also joined the marketing team. Granddaughter Amanda Parker is the general manager of the Fess Parker Wine Country Inn in Los Olivos. Grandson Kristopher Parker runs Third Window Brewing Company in nearby Santa Barbara.Multi-generational stewardship on the ranchFess Parker, who died in 2010, spent his later years working with his family on the property after leaving the film industry in the early 1970s. By keeping active family oversight across every part of the business, from managing vineyard soil to planning cattle breeding, the Parker family continues to operate the 714-acre estate as an integrated and largely self-sustaining working ranch.You use AI every day. articles.title: Trump says he would pardon admin officials before leaving White House, cites Biden pardons
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump said he would consider pre-emptively pardoning members of his administration before the end of his second term, telling Time
articles.body: US President Donald Trump said he would consider pre-emptively pardoning members of his administration before the end of his second term, telling Time magazine that he would have no issue granting clemency to officials who could face investigations or prosecution after he leaves office.“Yeah, sure I’d do that,” Trump said in the interview, published Thursday, when asked whether he would pardon members of his administration.Trump defended the possibility by pointing to former president Joe Biden’s use of pre-emptive pardons in the final hours of his presidency. “Sleepy Joe gave pardons to everybody,” Trump said, referring to Biden’s pardons for former Joint Chiefs of Staff chairman Mark Milley, Dr Anthony Fauci and members and staffers of the House committee that investigated the January 6, 2021, Capitol riot.Biden had issued the pardons amid concerns that Trump could target people who had been critical of him after returning to the White House.Biden also granted a sweeping pardon to his son Hunter Biden in December 2024, despite the administration previously saying he would not do so.Trump’s comments came as he discussed the possibility of Democrats regaining control of the House in the 2026 midterm elections and launching investigations into his administration.“They’ll probably go after me and I’ll go after them,” Trump told Time when asked how he was preparing for a possible Democratic House majority.The Wall Street Journal reported in April that Trump had repeatedly promised top administration officials they would receive pardons before he leaves office. According to the report, Trump had told officials he would pardon “everyone who has come within 200 feet of the Oval.”The issue of potential prosecutions of Trump administration officials has also gained attention amid Democratic calls for investigations into several members of his administration.Trump has already exercised his clemency powers extensively during his second term. On his first day back in office in January 2025, he pardoned or commuted the sentences of roughly 1,500 people charged in connection with the January 6 Capitol riot.Since then, Trump has issued about 170 additional pardons and commutations to people convicted of crimes, according to a list maintained by the US Justice Department.The House can impeach federal officials and hold them in contempt of Congress, though it does not have the power to bring criminal charges. A resolution seeking to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is also scheduled for a vote after the midterm elections.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: ‘Fatal point of no return’: Putin warns against use of nukes amid global tensions
articles.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday warned that the world was living through a dangerous moment, saying escalating international conflicts could
articles.body: Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday warned that the world was living through a dangerous moment, saying escalating international conflicts could reach a “fatal point of no return” and stressing that weapons of mass destruction must never be used.Speaking at the Valdai Forum of international Russia experts in Moscow, Putin said the world’s leading powers possessed arsenals capable of destroying all life or reducing the Earth to a “catastrophic state”.He urged countries to recognise how quickly escalating retaliation could lead to an irreversible situation.“We must realise that the moment when nothing can be changed any longer may come very quickly and unexpectedly for everyone. The logic of escalating, increasingly harsh retaliatory measures leads to a fatal point of no return,” Putin said.“At the heart of this escalation lie arrogance and overconfidence. This is a path to the brink of the abyss. All the more so today, when the arsenals of the world’s leading powers contain weapons capable of destroying all life or, at the very least, reducing the Earth to a catastrophic state. Can we be certain that these weapons will never be used? Well, of course not. We must bear this in mind and avoid such an outcome.”Putin warns of Western role in Ukraine conflictPutin said Ukraine would not be able to carry out attacks deep inside Russia without Western technical support, arguing that such assistance amounted to direct involvement in the conflict.He said Russia viewed attempts to use Ukraine as a proxy to fight Russia as a threat. Putin also said Moscow was not planning to attack factories in other countries that manufacture weapons for Ukraine, but warned that Russia's military and intelligence services needed to closely monitor them.“We are not going to attack tomorrow enterprises in countries which supply weapons to Ukraine, but that's a threat,” Putin said.Putin also said Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries had cost Russia 1% of its gross domestic product.He said Ukraine had “partially achieved its objectives” through the attacks, but added that Russia was responding in kind.He further said Ukraine had damaged more than 100 Russian vessels in the Black Sea and that Moscow was now responding.Russia issues warning over KaliningradPutin said Russia would consider using the full range of weapons in its arsenal if its Baltic exclave of Kaliningrad came under threat. He maintained that Russia did not plan to attack anyone but would respond to aggression.“We are not going to attack anyone, but will respond if we face aggression,” Putin said.Kaliningrad is a Russian territory on the Baltic Sea separated from mainland Russia by other countries and located between Nato members Poland and Lithuania. The region has become a focus of tensions between Moscow and the alliance.In a separate development on Thursday, the Kremlin said Russia's recent letter to Nato on Kaliningrad should not be viewed as confrontational. The document accused the alliance of pursuing a “dangerous and reckless course” carrying “high risks of the outbreak of a direct armed conflict”.Putin also said Russia was not threatening European countries and did not plan to attack them.“We are not threatening anyone and we do not plan to attack any European countries, not in 2030, not in 2050,” he said.Putin says global conflicts likely to continuePutin said international conflicts were likely to continue as the global order undergoes fundamental changes, although he said the situation would improve as what he described as Western hegemony waned.“Regardless of which scenario unfolds globally in the coming years, the continuation of international conflicts is, unfortunately, highly likely. This is due in part to the fact that ongoing fundamental shifts—and the opportunities they present—fuel ambitions and a willingness to take risks for the sake of a seemingly massive payoff,” Putin said.He again stressed the need to avoid catastrophic scenarios.Putin also said Russia supported a possible trilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump, although he said an agenda for such talks would first need to be worked out.On the Middle East, Putin said he hoped the Strait of Hormuz would remain open to shipping and that sanctions on Iran would be lifted. He also said Russia's proposals to deliver enriched uranium from Iran to Russia remained valid.Putin said Russia remained interested in cooperation with Japan but was concerned about what he described as the country's militarisation.He added that Japanese companies continued to operate in Russia and that Moscow supported them and others working with Russia.He also criticised military drills and arrests of Russian vessels as forms of escalation and said Russia had a competitive advantage in defending itself.You use AI every day. articles.summary: British counter-terrorism police have arrested a 27-year-old UK-Iranian dual national in connection with the security incident near RAF Fairford, as
articles.body: British counter-terrorism police have arrested a 27-year-old UK-Iranian dual national in connection with the security incident near RAF Fairford, as investigators examine possible foreign state involvement in the case.The man was arrested in Westminster, London, on Thursday on suspicion of preparing terrorist acts, Counter Terrorism Policing said, reported BBC. Police also questioned a 26-year-old British man under caution and searched two properties in the capital.The developments come days after five British men in their 20s were arrested near the Gloucestershire airbase on suspicion of explosives offences and later on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act. All five, who are from London, have since been released on police bail and remain under investigation.Counter-terrorism police said they were pursuing multiple lines of inquiry, including a possible foreign state connection. “The investigation into circumstances surrounding events in Gloucestershire is hugely complex, and our specialist teams are interrogating multiple lines of enquiry,” said Vicki Evans, the senior national coordinator for counter-terrorism policing.“As we’ve made clear, we’re looking at all possible angles - including possible foreign state involvement,” she added.The five men were arrested in the early hours of Sunday after police received reports of three suspicious vans travelling towards RAF Fairford. Searches of the vehicles found a quantity of petrol but no explosive devices, police said.The arrests triggered a major security operation around the base, which is used by the US Air Force and has supported American military operations in the Middle East, including the recent war with Iran. Police had initially suspected explosives offences before broadening the allegations to include preparation of a terrorist act.The investigation has also considered a possible Iranian connection. UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said there were “strong indications” that Iran played a role in the incident, while Tehran has denied involvement. US officials have also raised concerns over the case and the decision to release the five suspects on bail.Burnham has defended the decision, saying the suspects were released under strict conditions and that British authorities remained in close contact with their US counterparts.RAF Fairford, around 160 km west of London, has been used by US bombers during military operations in the Middle East. The base has also drawn threats from Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, which in July warned that British bases used for attacks on Iran could be considered legitimate targets. Iran has rejected claims linking it to the Fairford incident.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.body: An Indian man was arrested and charged with several sex crimes in Davidson County, North Carolina after it was found that he traveled from India to North Carolina to meet a girl with whom he claimed to be in a long-term online relationship. The girl was found to be 17 years old. 31-year-old Prit Pankaj Jain was speaking to the girl, hiding his age and presenting himself as a much younger person.According to the Davidson County Sheriff’s Office, they were called to the Meadowlands community on September 24 by an Uber driver, who had concerns about a passenger he had just dropped off in the area.Two weeks before Jain's arrival in North Carolina, the girl broke up with him and blocked him after she learned his real age. They had been chatting on all social media platforms for two years and Jain knew the girl's address. After the girl broke up with him, he threatened that he would release all explicit material they had exchanged.The sheriff’s office says that Jain groomed the victim online. The warrants state that he had recorded videos of the victim engaging in sexual activity. He was charged with four counts of first-degree exploitation of a minor, four counts of third-degree exploitation of a minor and one count of sexual extortion and given no bond.When the police reached the spot and made contact with Jain, he told them that he wanted to leave gifts for his girlfriend. Deputies then discovered that the girlfriend he was referring to was a juvenile."Investigators determined that Jain subsequently traveled from his home in Mumbai, India, to the United States in an attempt to re-establish contact with the female juvenile," the sheriff's office said. The investigators believed that Jain was also aware of a secondary address for other family members.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: In 2013, Rob Scheer began packing backpacks at his dining table after recalling carrying his belongings in trash bags as a foster child; his charity has distributed 300,000+ backpacks
articles.summary: A simple effort around a dining table, started in 2013 to protect the dignity of children entering foster care, has grown into an international charity
articles.body: A simple effort around a dining table, started in 2013 to protect the dignity of children entering foster care, has grown into an international charity that has provided essential items to hundreds of thousands of young people. Rob Scheer began packing backpacks at home after seeing his newly adopted foster children arrive carrying their belongings in black plastic rubbish bags. Scheer remembered his own childhood in the foster care system and decided to end the practice by starting Comfort Cases. According to official impact figures from Comfort Cases, the nonprofit has distributed more than 300,000 Comfort Cases and Comfort XL duffel bags to children in foster care across all 50 US states, Washington, D.C., Puerto Rico and the United Kingdom. Comfort Cases says its first Packing Party took place in December 2013.Childhood memories trigger community actionScheer grew up in the American foster care system during the 1970s. When he aged out at 18, he was given a black trash bag containing his few belongings and had to begin adult life on his own. Comfort Cases says he had also carried a trash bag when he first entered foster care. Years later, after marrying his husband Reece and choosing to build a family through foster adoption, Scheer saw the same thing happen again. Their adopted children arrived at their home carrying their clothes and belongings in plastic trash bags. Comfort Cases says Rob and Reece were shocked that the practice was still common decades after Rob had experienced it himself. The experience pushed Scheer to act. He brought his family together at their dining room table in Maryland and began packing backpacks with basic care items for children in foster care. The first community Packing Party was held in December 2013, and Comfort Cases was soon established as an official 501(c)(3) nonprofit. In background information published by Comfort Cases, Scheer explains that children should not have to carry their belongings in something meant for trash. The charity's goal is to replace those bags with new backpacks and duffel bags that children can keep as their own.What goes inside a comfort caseSocial workers may need to move children between homes with little warning, sometimes during the night. Comfort Cases was created to give children their own bags and basic items when they enter foster care. The charity provides bags for children of different ages, from babies through young adults. Its cases are filled with new items meant to provide comfort and basic personal care.According to information published by Comfort Cases, a typical case includes:A brand-new backpack or small duffel bag New pajamas, from infant sizes through adult sizesA new fleece blanketPersonal care items, including a toothbrush, toothpaste, shampoo, soap and other toiletriesA new book or activity book suited to the child's ageA stuffed animal for younger childrenA journal for older childrenComfort Cases says its items are new. Its current materials describe the bags as containing brand-new essentials, including pajamas, toiletries, toothbrushes and toothpaste, books or activities, journals, stuffed animals and blankets. The goal is to help children feel that their belongings matter and that they have something that belongs to them. The charity's materials emphasize that the items are not used or passed down from another child.Nationwide reach and volunteer networksWhat started as a family effort quickly grew as volunteers and community groups joined the work. Today, Comfort Cases operates from its headquarters in Gaithersburg, Maryland, and works with child welfare agencies and other organizations to get the bags to children in foster care. The charity's impact figures show that it has reached all 50 states, Washington, D.C., Puerto Rico and the United Kingdom. According to Comfort Cases, community events known as "Packing Parties" bring volunteers together to fill backpacks with essential items. Businesses, schools, religious groups and other community organizations can take part in these events. The charity has also expanded beyond the United States. Comfort Cases says its United Kingdom operation, Comfort Cases UK, launched in 2022.Pushing for legislative changeBeyond giving children bags and personal items, Scheer has also worked to change policies around foster care. Comfort Cases says Scheer has used his public platform to push for an end to the use of trash bags for children entering foster care. The organization says its work has also helped support laws banning trash bags in foster care placements. According to Comfort Cases, Maryland and Texas passed laws banning the use of trash bags in foster care placements in 2023. The organization says other states, including New York and Oregon, have also been considering similar changes. As of 2026, Comfort Cases continues to expand its partnerships with child welfare organizations. Its stated goal remains to make sure children entering foster care receive a proper bag filled with new essentials instead of having to carry their belongings in a plastic trash bag.You use AI every day. articles.title: Meet Heléna Muirhead-Hunt, the student who discovered a new fossil species 551 million years old, linked to ancient comb-jellies
articles.summary: A Memorial palaeobiology graduate student has discovered a new fossil species in rocks from Newfoundland that are dated to 551 million years old.
articles.body: A Memorial palaeobiology graduate student has discovered a new fossil species in rocks from Newfoundland that are dated to 551 million years old. Heléna Muirhead-Hunt found the fossils at Inner Meadow in Upper Island Cove, a site known for preserving soft-bodied organisms without shells or bones. According to Memorial University’s Gazette, most fossils found there belong to the Ediacara biota, which includes proto-animals such as fractal-like rangeomorphs.She said, “But when we uncovered the first specimen of our new fossil, we knew that we were onto something really special.” Her supervisor, Dr Duncan McIlroy, suggested comparing it with ctenophores, also known as comb-jellies. The new species has been named Edrathina obditchia.How Heléna Muirhead-Hunt found a 551-million-year-old fossilHeléna Muirhead-Hunt found the new fossils at Inner Meadow in Upper Island Cove, Newfoundland. The site contains Ediacaran-aged rocks dated to 551 million years old and is known for the exceptional preservation of soft-bodied organisms without shells or bones. Most fossils at the site belong to the Ediacara biota of proto-animals, including the fractal-like rangeomorphs for which Newfoundland is known.When Muirhead-Hunt uncovered the first specimen of the new fossil, she showed it to her supervisor, Dr. Duncan McIlroy. He suggested that she compare it with ctenophores, an important group of organisms also known as comb-jellies. The oldest known ctenophores were 20 million years younger than the fossils Muirhead-Hunt had discovered at Inner Meadow.What makes the fossil different from modern comb-jelliesThe fossils were found to be closest to a group of stem-ctenophores known from the much younger Burgess Shale fossil site in British Columbia. Modern comb-jellies are centimetre-sized blobs of jelly with longitudinal comb-rows that shimmer in waves of rainbow colours when they swim. Their ancient relatives, known as stem-ctenophores, were sedentary.Ctenophores are important to biologists and palaeontologists because scientists have long studied their place in the history of animals. Scientists have puzzled over what might have been the earliest animal ancestor since Darwin’s time. Sponges were long considered the simplest animals. More recently, scientists have debated whether sponges or ctenophores came first in the history of animals, a question researchers have argued mostly on genetic evidence.Why Edrathina obditchia is important to the fossil recordThe new fossil species has been named Edrathina obditchia. Muirhead-Hunt said, “Since we know the Beothuk word for comb is “Edrathin” and “Obditch” is beast, combining them into the new name seemed like a fitting tribute to the culturally extinct Beothuk people of Newfoundland”. Muirhead-Hunt and McIlroy note that the fossils were closest to stem-ctenophores. Their finding is significant because the oldest known ctenophores were 20 million years younger, leaving a gap in the fossil record.The new fossil and the history of early animalsThe discovery provides new fossil evidence to the debate over the earliest animal ancestor. Sponges were once considered likely leading possibilities because modern sponges have a simple body plan without muscles or a nervous system. However, scientists found that sponges have inactive genetic coding for these animal characteristics, raising questions about how primitive they really are.Another hypothesis suggests that ctenophores may have branched from the animal tree of life before sponges evolved. Much of this debate has focused on genetic evidence. Until now, the lack of Ediacaran ctenophore fossils left an important gap in the fossil record. Muirhead-Hunt said the team believes the new fossil may help fill this 20-million-year gap in the history of ctenophores.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: 'INDIA Bloc stands united and will move forward collectively....it is not about individual decisions': Mamata
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: A day after the INDIA Alliance announced a joint agitation to demand the resignation of Gyanesh Kumar over the SIR exercise, Trinamool Congress
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A day after the INDIA Alliance announced a joint agitation to demand the resignation of Gyanesh Kumar over the SIR exercise, Trinamool Congress Chairperson and former West Bengal CM Mamata Banerjee said that for the Opposition this was a “collective” fight and shared that she had promptly responded to CPI(M) general secretary MA Baby last week when he reached out to her over the working of the Election Commission as it was a "national issue".Reports of the interaction between Baby and Banerjee had attracted much attention last week as it saw two parties with decades-long differences in Bengal coming together on the question of the Election Commission (EC).Banerjee shared details of the interaction and the sentiment behind both sides putting aside their differences and coming together, while responding to questions at a press conference in Delhi. Party national general secretary Abhishek Banerjee and senior party leaders Derek O' Brien, Dola Sen, Mahua Moitra, Menaka Guruswamy and Saket Gokhale were among those present with Mamata Banerjee at the press conference.“Our position is that when Constitutional institutions and democratic rights are at stake, political parties should examine the issue beyond their individual colours and interests,” Banerjee asserted.When asked about Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, the question of leadership of the opposition alliance and her view on who can be the Bloc's PM candidate, the TMC Chairperson said, "INDIA Alliance is United and together. It is not about individual decisions. We are like a family, and we will decide collectively on these issues.""Regional political parties have their own circumstances and compulsions, and we understand that. We maintain good relations with leaders such as Arvind Kejriwal (AAP), Nitish Kumar (JDU) and MK Stalin (DMK), while local political decisions may differ from state to state. Sometimes, INDIA's alliance partners may not attend a particular programme because of local political considerations, but that does not necessarily mean there is disagreement on broader national issues,” she added.“We are with the INDIA alliance, and whatever decisions the alliance takes, we will respect them like a family and work together with unity. Our priority is to stand together and move forward collectively,” Banerjee said.“2029 is still far away; first, look at what is happening in 2027. “Khela toh ab hoga” — the real political game begins now. You never know what may happen in the next two, three, or six months. Politics can change very quickly, and we will continue to watch the situation, remain united and make decisions together as an alliance,” she emphasised.“It is important for Gyanesh Kumar to go...change is critical at this stage to make way for a free and fair electoral system,” Banerjee said in response to a question about whether the resignation of CEC would help resolve the systemic problems.TMC national general secretary and Lok Sabha MP Abhishek Banerjee lashed out, saying, "When questions are directed at Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar or the Election Commission, I believe the answers should come from the Election Commission itself. Instead, we repeatedly see BJP leaders responding to those questions. My point is simple: constitutional authorities must answer legitimate questions themselves and place facts before the public rather than allowing political parties to speak on their behalf." articles.title: Mental capacity in question, HC backs Pocso case closure
articles.summary: Bombay HC’s Nagpur bench asks Bhandara court to reconsider closing a POCSO case, citing CrPC 329-330 and accused’s mild intellectual disability.
articles.body: Nagpur: After finding that an accused is incapable of independently defending himself due to mild intellectual disability, the Nagpur bench of Bombay High Court last week asked Bhandara Sessions Court to reconsider his plea seeking closure of a POCSO case against him.Justice Mehroz Pathan set aside the Aug 4, 2025, order rejecting the discharge plea of the accused and directed the trial court to determine in two months whether there is sufficient prima facie material in the chargesheet to proceed against him.The trial court has also been directed to consider whether the accused can be released under Section 330(3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, keeping in view the nature of the alleged acts and the extent of his mental incapacity.The accused is facing prosecution under Sections 323, 354 and 354A of IPC read with Sections 8, 10 and 12 of POCSO Act in connection with a case registered at Tumsar police station in Nov 2023. The offences against him included using criminal force against a woman with intent to outrage her modesty and sexual assault on a child.HC’s direction followed its examination of a psychiatric assessment report and evidence of three doctors who after examination had recorded that he was suffering from mild intellectual disability.Justice Pathan noted that all doctors had consistently stated that the accused was unable to understand the consequences of his actions and could not independently defend himself.One doctor stated that the accused’s IQ was 68 and that he was unable to defend himself in a criminal case. Another testified that he could not understand questions or provide rational answers. He also stated that while the accused’s physical age was 20 at the time of examination, his mental age was around 14.“The findings recorded by the sessions judge that there is no consistent opinion of all the doctors that the accused is of unsound mind, is perverse,” Justice Pathan observed.The court said the trial court had failed to properly apply the provisions of Sections 329 and 330 of CrPC, which prescribe the procedure where an accused is found to be of unsound mind and incapable of entering a defence.HC directed the sessions court to first determine whether the prosecution material establishes a prima facie case and thereafter deal with the accused in accordance with Section 330(3), which permits the court to consider release based on the nature of the alleged act and the extent of mental incapacity.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Nagpur | Silver Rate in Nagpur | Bank Holidays in Nagpur | Public Holidays in Nagpur | Petrol Price in Nagpur | Diesel Price in Nagpur | CNG Price in Nagpur | LPG Price in NagpurStay updated with the latest Nagpur news. articles.title: KTC breaks 46-year gender barrier with first woman bus driver
articles.summary: Kadamba Transport Corporation breaks 46-year barrier, hiring Pooja Vaingankar as its first woman heavy-vehicle bus driver; joining after medical formalities.
articles.body: Panaji: For nearly five decades since the Kadamba Transport Corporation (KTC) was established in 1980, the steering wheel of its public transport buses has remained overwhelmingly a man’s domain. That is set to change with the induction of Pooja Vaingankar (32) who will become the first woman heavy-vehicle driver recruited by the state-run corporation.Vaingankar, however, is not stepping into the heavy-vehicle world as a novice. She already has experience driving goods vehicles on interstate routes, a background that helped her stand out during KTC’s selection process.“It feels very exciting to know that I have been selected,” she said.“Women have been driving cars and bikes for years but rarely do we see representation from the female gender in this line of work. I struggled while growing up so I always had the urge to be self-sufficient. I had always been fond of cars and had learnt how to drive from a person who I consider to be my guru. Eventually, the transition from cars to trucks happened and before I knew it, there came an opportunity to work for a private company as a goods carrier driver, and I took it up. After a few years of doing so when KTC opened vacancies, I decided to apply and got shortlisted.”For 46 years, women interested in driving KTC’s heavy vehicles have had to contend with the perception that the job is physically demanding, technically difficult and inherently suited to men. Vaingankar’s journey challenges that assumption by placing an experienced woman in the driver’s seat of a state-run public transport corporation.KTC managing director Rohan Khaskar described her as a talented driver and said her driving abilities, including her technical handling of a heavy vehicle, were assessed during the selection process.“Unlike someone learning to handle a heavy vehicle for the first time, she has been driving trucks for several years. Her experience includes driving between Goa and Belgaum, giving her familiarity with long-distance heavy-vehicle operations. That experience could prove valuable as she makes the transition to passenger transport,” Khaskar told TOI.The precise route on which Vaingankar will be deployed has not yet been finalised. KTC officials said she could be assigned a route convenient for her, considering that she is based in Bicholim. Possibilities include a regular daytime shuttle or routes such as Margao-bound services, depending on the route she is comfortable operating.Her first day behind the wheel of a KTC bus is expected only after the ongoing recruitment and medical formalities are completed.“KTC is currently completing medical tests for a larger intake of personnel, with approximately 250 conductors and 100 drivers forming part of the recruitment process. Vaingankar will therefore be joining the services along with the rest of them from next week onwards,” Khaskar said.Her appointment comes at a time when KTC’s workforce is gradually becoming more gender-diverse, with nearly 40 women conductors and four new women traffic controllers already part of its ranks. articles.title: Optimistic ride: Kochi cousins sail into Asian Games silver
articles.summary: Kochi cousins Prince Noble and Manu Francis win Asian Games men’s skiff silver for India, the nation’s first sailing silver and first medal since 2018.
articles.body: Kochi: When Prince Noble was five, he nonchalantly climbed aboard a boat named Optimistic and sailed off the Vypeen coast here with his father, Noble K G, and a few cousins. He could not have known then how apt the name would prove to be.Twenty-five years later, optimism, along with skill, carried Havildar Prince, 30, and his cousin, Naik Manu Francis, 31, both of the Indian Army, to silver in the men’s skiff event at the Asian Games. It was India’s first silver in sailing and its first medal in the event since a bronze in 2018.India led going into the final day but could not hold off China. “A combination of factors went against us. There was pressure on us to sustain our lead coming into today, but silver is what we have to settle for,” Prince told TOI.The contest was decided over nine races, with the lowest aggregate score winning. The Indian pair finished with 23 points, behind China’s Wen Zaiding and Liu Tian, who took gold with 16.Prince is from Vypeen and Manu from Varappuzha. The maternal cousins grew up in fishing families along the Keralam coast. “My father was a fisherman and the sea is near our home. So, we are connected to it. That is why it was easy for us to start with sailing,” Prince said.Their introduction to the sport was anything but technical. “At first we didn’t know anything about sailing. We thought it was like swimming and playing in the water,” he recalled.A turning point came in 2008, when Kochi hosted the Volvo Ocean Race at Willingdon Island. Manu finished first and Prince second. They joined the Indian Army in 2014 and began taking sailing seriously, training at the Mumbai Yachting Node. They won bronze at the 2023 Asian Championships in Abu Dhabi.“We grew up together. Over the years, there’s an understanding between us,” Manu said. Their coach, Sandeep Jain, a retired sub-officer who coaches the 49er team, calls the cousins “dedicated and hardworking” who do not see sailing “as a chore”.Prince’s father, who played a key role in evacuation efforts during the 2018 deluge, died a year later after a leg injury suffered during the operation failed to heal. “I dedicate my silver medal to my father. I’m sure I have made him proud,” he said.His mother, Bindu Noble, called the win “a blessing from the Almighty”. Prince sounded disappointed at missing out on gold, she said, but added: “I just want him to come back home and spend time here. I rarely get to see him these days. Training and competitions keep him in Spain and Germany.”Jain believes the silver is only the beginning. “Their time is still to come,” he said.
